clue.text: Organ for which I'll pay and get ultimately some hard puzzles?

definitions.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical voicing a view

indicators.note: puzzles is read as a verb, so the words before it are confounded and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word some

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reader grumbles that they pay for a paper only to be handed fiendish puzzles at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzles' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal; 'ultimately' takes the E ending 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a publication speaking for a group; this London broadsheet is one, and it printed the puzzle.

clue.text: I got collar made out of skin

indicators.note: made out here suggests something rearranged, so the preceding letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a collar crafted from leather hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out of skin' reads as material; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'of skin' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermatology is the medical study of the skin, so this adjective relates to skin.

clue.text: Change ending in film, oddly, with treatment from 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest'

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word film

parts.words: treatment from 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest'
parts.note: electroconvulsive therapy, ECT, is the shock treatment shown in that film

explanation.surface: A film critic notes a changed ending to the movie about a psychiatric ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change ending' looks like an alteration to the film's conclusion; it is the grammatical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflect a word is to alter its suffix for tense, number or case, i.e. to vary its termination.

clue.text: Old European chap turning up with big John and his Scottish cousin?

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a chap is a guy
OS is outsize, a clothing label for big
john is slang for a toilet, as is lav
Ian is the Scottish form of the name John

explanation.surface: A man of the Balkans arrives with a large John and his relative from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name but is the toilet; then 'his Scottish cousin' treats John as a name after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the former Balkan federation dissolved in the 1990s is an old European nationality.

clue.text: Make no mistake, France's in on European summit

parts.note: en is the French word for in
sur is French for on, continuing the France's theme

indicators.note: summit in a down clue is the top letter of the word European

explanation.surface: A diplomat insists France takes part at the European leaders' meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France's' covers both 'in' and 'on', which are translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something is to leave no room for error, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Swiss produce them, half going 'cuckoo'

indicators.note: half going means the first half of the word them is dropped

parts.note: cuckoo means crazy, mental

explanation.surface: The Swiss make cuckoo clocks, half of which are going cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss produce' hints at clocks; it is a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: This holey cheese is made in Switzerland, so it is an example of that nation's produce.

clue.text: Manage succession

definitions.meaning: to ... a business is to manage it
a ... of wins is a succession of them

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both operating something and an unbroken series, two separate senses.

clue.text: One supporting left — Communists' fifth columns

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts one piece directly below another

parts.note: port is the nautical left
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a fifth of the ten letters in the word Communists is its opening pair

explanation.surface: A left-wing backer mentions communist fifth columnists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifth columns' suggests fifth columnists; 'fifth' takes the first two of the ten letters of 'Communists'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch whose roof rests on a row of pillars, so it is defined by its columns.

clue.text: Taking decisive action, make reparations to court about upland parking

parts.note: to atone is to make amends
fells are upland moors in northern England
to woo is to court a sweetheart
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone decisively pays compensation to a court over a hillside car park.
explanation.walkthrough: FELLS are high moors of the English Lake District and Pennines.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means all in one sudden stroke, describing a single bold action.

clue.text: Right smoky atmosphere obstructs view over shelters

indicators.note: obstructs puts the smoky air in the way, inside the view word
over signals the view word is turned round

parts.note: to view is to see
a fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere

explanation.surface: Smoke hanging in the air blocks the view across a row of huts.
explanation.definitionFit: Places of safety from danger or pursuit are havens, the plural noun matching.

clue.text: Tower Colliery painting exhibition opening put back

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word exhibition, standing at the end of the colliery word, is moved further back

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine
art is painting put on show

explanation.surface: A mining-town art show is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening put back' looks like a delayed launch; the E (the opening of 'exhibition') shifts two places later in MINEART.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Vote for first person in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the word is identified by how it sounds

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A judge casts a yes vote for the first performer at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a talent try-out; here it simply means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary voters say this word to register a yes, so it is a vote in favour.

clue.text: Well advanced, one's old — not primarily a candidate for 'salad days'?

parts.note: a spring is a well or water source
on means forward, advanced
one's read as one is, giving the numeral I

indicators.note: primarily selects the first letter of the word not

explanation.surface: An elderly person, well on in years, is no longer a candidate for youthful salad days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salad days' means youth, but the definition takes it literally: something that goes in a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: This mild young allium is eaten raw in salads, so it is literally fit for salad days.

clue.text: Report says abandoning the breast in too many cases is excessive

indicators.note: a report spoken aloud tells us the following words are judged by sound

parts.words: abandoning the breast in too many cases
parts.note: over-weaning would be taking too many babies off breast milk

explanation.surface: A health report finds too many mothers give up breastfeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Overweening describes arrogance or presumption that goes beyond due bounds, hence immoderate.

clue.text: Expression of sympathy after openly gay lecturer gets ban

indicators.note: after means the sympathy word comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: someone who is out is openly gay
aw is a cry of sympathy

explanation.surface: A gay academic is barred, prompting cries of sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to prohibit it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Slowly fade one recording on disc that's very loud

parts.note: a taper is one who tapes, i.e. records
O is a disc shape
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A deafening record fades out gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper off is to diminish gradually, like sound slowly dying away.

clue.text: Northern city, they say

parts.note: the capital of Finland, said as two words, sounds like a hellish place being pitch-black

explanation.walkthrough: Split 4,4, the city's name sounds like a phrase saying the underworld is black as ink; 'they say' flags that spoken reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Finland's capital lies far north on the Baltic, so it is a northern capital.

clue.text: Sketched broad principles of devolution, revised after losing 50 per cent of vote

indicators.note: revised means the remaining letters are reworked into a fresh order
losing means those letters are taken out of the word devolution
50 per cent of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A devolution plan is revised after losing half the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes VO, half of 'vote', from DEVOLUTION; 'revised' then rearranges DEUTLION.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline a plan is to sketch its main features without detail.

clue.text: Fish it up with a pail? Tricky

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word it is read upwards
tricky suggests the letters of a pail are jumbled

explanation.surface: Catching a fish with a bucket proves tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilapia is a freshwater cichlid widely farmed for food, so it is a fish.

clue.text: Turn partners back to front at beginning of line

indicators.note: back to front moves the final letter of the partners word to its front

parts.note: wives are marriage partners

indicators.note: at beginning of picks the first letter of the word line

explanation.surface: At a dance, partners change places at the head of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to pivot or rotate on a point, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Artist from Glasgow area bringing up the rear should take tips from Gainsborough

indicators.note: the first two letters of the district name are sent to its rear

parts.note: Govan is a district of Glasgow

indicators.note: tips from takes the two ends of the word Gainsborough

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian painter, last in line, should learn from Gainsborough.
explanation.walkthrough: GOVAN is a shipbuilding district of Glasgow in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch post-impressionist who painted Sunflowers is a famous painter.

clue.text: Exercises involving 50 and 60 per cent of Asian opponents

indicators.note: 50 here means half of a six-letter island name is kept

parts.note: Taiwan and China are rival Asian states

indicators.note: 60 per cent of a five-letter country name keeps its first three letters

parts.note: Taiwan and China are rival Asian states

explanation.surface: A workout drawing on fractions of two Asian rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives both pieces: Taiwan and the mainland that claims it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese martial art is practised as a series of slow, flowing exercise movements.

clue.text: Shoe wheeled out takes after popular range

indicators.note: after places the jumbled piece behind the others

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a range of products is a line

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of takes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wheeled shoe is brought out, coming after a popular product range.
explanation.definitionFit: This boot has its wheels set in a single row, so it is footwear on wheels.

clue.text: Cons of 'Go West, Young Man'?

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a son is a young male child

explanation.surface: The drawbacks of the old advice to seek a fortune out west.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous American advice 'Go West, young man' becomes instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative votes or arguments against, as in pros and cons, are refusals.

clue.text: Right to have one in case of awful pains?

definitions.text: Right to have one in case of awful pains?

indicators.note: in case of means the letters go inside a casing
awful signals the letters of pains are mangled

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: It is right to take a painkiller when suffering awful aches.
explanation.definitionFit: A common painkilling tablet is what one reaches for to ease aches.

clue.text: Outfit to fix e.g. election

definitions.meaning: a set of clothes or gear
to ... a vote is to fix it fraudulently

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a costume or kit and the act of manipulating a result dishonestly.

clue.text: Who's the winner when Cambridge University current second team takes on Oxford's first?

parts.note: CU abbreviates Cambridge University
I is the physics symbol for current
the B team is a second team
taken as written

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word Oxford

explanation.surface: A Varsity match: Cambridge's reserves take on Oxford's first team; who wins?
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin tag means 'to whose benefit?', asked when seeking who gains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin question asks who benefits, i.e. who profits from an event.

clue.text: Disallow winning shot that might give one counter-advantage?

parts.note: to bar is to forbid
gaining means winning
a chip is a lofted golf shot

explanation.surface: A referee disallows a winning golf shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' hints at a gambling chip used to negotiate.
explanation.definitionFit: A concession held in reserve gives leverage in negotiations, like a casino token at the table.
